glosses.primary_gloss: to pass down and carry on
glosses.notes: Used for traditions, skills, values, or practices that are inherited and then actively continued by later people.

examples.meaning_en: to pass down and carry on
examples.sentence: 老师退休前把做椅子的方法一点一点传承给两个年轻人，怕再过几年就没人愿意继续学了。
村里那座老戏台本来快拆了，后来几个年轻人回来帮忙，才把过年过节唱戏的习惯慢慢传承下来。
母亲常说，家里真正该传承的不是旧东西，而是有事也肯先让别人把话说完的做法。

example_translations.translation: Before retiring, the teacher passed down the method for making chairs step by step to two young learners, worried that in a few more years no one would still be willing to keep learning it.
The old village opera stage was originally about to be torn down, but after several young people came back to help, the custom of performing there during holiday seasons was slowly carried forward.
Mother often says that what a family should really pass down is not old things, but the habit of still letting other people finish speaking first when something happens.

glosses.notes: Means passing along information, feelings, orders, or attitudes so that other people receive them clearly.

examples.sentence: 经理怕电话里说不清，就让秘书把最新安排写成一张纸，一个一个传达到还在路上的同事那里。
他没有直接生气，只是把杯子轻轻放下，可是大家还是都听懂了他想传达的不满。
广播一响，工作人员立刻把停电通知传达到每一层，连还在门口等消息的人都很快退开了。

example_translations.translation: Afraid the message would not be clear over the phone, the manager had the secretary write the latest arrangement on a sheet of paper and pass it along one by one to the coworkers still on the road.
He did not show anger directly and only set his cup down lightly, but everyone still understood the dissatisfaction he wanted to convey.
The moment the announcement came on, the staff immediately communicated the power-outage notice to every floor, and even the people still waiting by the door for news stepped back quickly.

glosses.notes: Most often describes illness spreading from one person to another, but it can also be used for emotions or moods that spread quickly.

examples.sentence: 医生提醒家长，孩子刚发烧那两天最容易传染，哪怕看着精神还行，也最好先别送回教室。
她只是咳了几下，旁边的人就已经离她远一点，怕自己也被传染。
紧张这种情绪有时也会传染，台上一个人忘词以后，后台等着的人说话都比刚才小心了。

example_translations.translation: The doctor reminded the parents that the first two days after a child develops a fever are when it spreads most easily, so even if the child still seems energetic, it is better not to send them back to class yet.
She only coughed a few times, but the person beside her had already moved a little farther away, afraid of getting infected too.
A tense mood can spread too. After one person on stage forgot the lines, the people waiting backstage all started speaking more carefully than before.

glosses.notes: Refers to diseases that can spread from person to person or through other forms of contact or exposure.

examples.sentence: 医院门口新贴的牌子提醒大家，春天有些传染病看着像普通感冒，可是排队时最好还是把距离留开。
奶奶年轻时见过传染病流行，所以一听说楼里有人持续发烧，就先把家里常用的杯子分开放好。
学校开会的时候，医生没有先讲成绩，而是先讲最近几种传染病怎么预防，怕班里的孩子一个接一个生病。

example_translations.translation: A newly posted sign at the hospital entrance reminds everyone that in spring some infectious diseases can look like an ordinary cold, but it is still best to keep some distance while waiting in line.
Grandma saw contagious diseases spread when she was young, so the moment she heard that someone in the building had an ongoing fever, she first separated the cups the family uses every day.

At the school meeting, the doctor did not talk about grades first, but instead explained how to prevent several recent infectious diseases because the children in the class could fall sick one after another.

glosses.notes: Used when knowledge, methods, skills, or experience are taught to someone in a deliberate and often generous way.

examples.sentence: 老教练不肯只让学生照着做，而是边示范边把什么时候该收力、什么时候该发力的感觉都传授给他们。
母亲做点心时总怕我只记住步骤，所以会一边量面粉，一边把省时间的小办法慢慢传授给我。
大家都喜欢这个护士，因为她肯把照顾病人的办法一点一点传授给新同事。

example_translations.translation: The old coach would not let the students merely copy the movements. Instead, while demonstrating, he imparted to them the sense of when to hold back strength and when to apply it.
When Mother makes pastries, she worries that I will remember only the steps, so while measuring the flour she slowly teaches me the little tricks that save time.
Everyone likes this nurse because she is willing to pass the methods for caring for patients on to new coworkers little by little.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to data, signals, images, or other information being sent from one place, device, or system to another.

examples.sentence: 车一进地下那段路，手机里的文件就一直传输不过去，急得他只好下车重新找信号。
工程师检查了一圈以后发现，不是机器停了，而是楼顶那根旧线让画面传输时一会儿有一会儿没有。
会议开始前，工作人员先把视频传输到后排的屏幕上，免得正式开始时前面的人能看见，后面的人却只听见声音。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the vehicle entered the underground stretch of road, the file on his phone would not transfer through, and he got so anxious that he had to get out and look for a signal again.
After checking everything, the engineer discovered that the machine itself had not stopped. It was the old cable on the roof that caused the image transmission to appear and disappear.

Before the meeting began, the staff first transmitted the video to the screen in the back so that once things formally started, the people in front would not be able to see it while the people in back could only hear the sound.

glosses.notes: Can refer to a faxed document, the act of faxing, or the machine used to send and receive faxed pages.

examples.sentence: 合同改完以后，客户还是坚持先收一份传真，所以秘书只好守在机器旁边，一页一页确认有没有卡纸。
老厂长到现在还习惯把价格表发传真过去，因为他总觉得电话里说得再快，也没有盖了章的纸让人放心。
他们早不看传真了，可是父亲还是把号写在纸上，怕以后要用。

example_translations.translation: After the contract was revised, the client still insisted on receiving a fax first, so the secretary had no choice but to stay beside the machine and check page by page for paper jams.

The old factory director still has the habit of sending the price list by fax, because he always feels that no matter how quickly something is explained over the phone, a stamped sheet of paper is more reassuring.
They no longer look at faxes, but Father still wrote the number on paper in case it would be needed later.

glosses.notes: A fairly formal collective word for ships and boats moving on the water, especially in transport, rescue, or port situations.

examples.sentence: 大雾刚起的时候，海上那几只船只都不敢再往前开，只能开着灯慢慢等前面的情况重新清楚起来。
救援队赶到时，旁边的船只已经主动让出一条路，好让救人的小船先靠过去把受伤的人接下来。
这片水道白天看着很宽，可是晚上来往船只一多，连站在岸边指挥的人都得一遍一遍拿灯提醒方向。

example_translations.translation: When the thick fog first rose, the ships out on the sea did not dare keep moving forward and could only leave their lights on while slowly waiting for the conditions ahead to become clear again.
By the time the rescue team arrived, the vessels at the side had already made room on their own so that the small rescue boat could come alongside first and take the injured person off.

This channel looks very wide in daylight, but once many ships are coming and going at night, even the people standing on shore directing them have to raise their lights again and again to signal the way.

glosses.notes: Often refers to something linked together in a string or chain, and it is also used as a measure word for items threaded or grouped in that way.

examples.sentence: 老板怕一忙就分不清谁点了什么，便先把每一串烤好的东西分开放好，再一盘一盘送出去。
她从夜市回来时手上还提着一串小灯，刚进门就把家里本来冷清的角落照得热闹了很多。
孩子看了半天，最后还是买了一串葡萄，拿在手里一直舍不得吃。

example_translations.translation: Afraid of mixing up who had ordered what once things got busy, the owner first separated each string of cooked food and then sent them out plate by plate.

When she came back from the night market, she was still carrying a string of little lights in her hand, and the moment she came in she made the corner at home that had felt cold and empty look much livelier.
The child looked around for a long time, but in the end still bought a bunch of grapes and held them in hand for a long time without wanting to eat them.

glosses.notes: Commonly refers either to a physical window opening or to a service counter where people line up to handle paperwork or payments.

examples.sentence: 排到窗口时，他才发现自己把证件落在另一件外套里，只好先让后面的人过去，自己跑到门口给家里打电话。
雨太大，办公室的窗口没有关严，靠墙那排资料很快就被风吹得乱成一团。
医院收费窗口一到中午就特别忙，所以护士总提醒第一次来的人先把单子填完整，别排到了又临时回去改。

example_translations.translation: Only when he reached the service window did he realize he had left his ID in another coat, so he had to let the person behind him go first and run to the entrance to call home.
The rain was so heavy that the office window had not been shut properly, and the row of materials against the wall was soon blown into a complete mess.

The hospital payment window gets especially busy at noon, so the nurses always remind first-time visitors to fill out their forms completely before lining up, so they do not reach the front and then have to go back and change something.

glosses.notes: Can describe forcing your way into a place, charging through something risky, or boldly going to a new place to try your luck.

examples.sentence: 保安刚把门拉开一点，一个抱着东西的人就想往里闯，嘴里还不停说自己只耽误两分钟。
父亲年轻时一个人闯到外地找工作，后来每次看见孩子怕吃苦，他都忍不住多说几句。
红灯刚亮，那辆车还是从人群前面闯过去，吓得正在过街的老人站在原地半天没敢动。

example_translations.translation: The security guard had only just pulled the door open a little when a man carrying things tried to barge in, still insisting that he would take only two minutes.
When Father was young, he ventured out to another place alone to look for work, and afterward whenever he sees a child afraid of hardship, he cannot help saying a few extra words.
The light had just turned red, but that car still rushed past the front of the crowd, frightening the older man in the crosswalk so badly that he stood frozen in place for quite a while.

glosses.notes: Used for starting an organization, school, company, publication, or other undertaking and getting it up and running.

examples.sentence: 这家小出版社刚创办的时候，办公室只有两张桌子，可是每个人都记得第一本书卖出去那天谁先红了眼圈。
她一直想创办一个给老人教手机的周末班，所以下了班就往社区跑，慢慢把愿意来帮忙的人一个个记下来。
父亲当年创办工厂不是因为手里有很多钱，而是看见镇上年轻人总得外出，心里一直放不下。

example_translations.translation: When this small publishing house was first founded, the office had only two desks, but everyone still remembers who got teary-eyed first on the day the first book was sold.

She has always wanted to start a weekend class that teaches older people how to use smartphones, so after work she keeps going to the neighborhood center and slowly writing down the names of people willing to help.
Father did not establish the factory back then because he had a lot of money in hand, but because he kept seeing the young people in town having to leave and could never stop worrying about it.

glosses.notes: Used for creating something new such as a system, structure, model, platform, or explanatory framework.

examples.sentence: 新同事花了一个下午才把共享文件夹创建好，还顺手把每一类资料分开命名，免得大家以后越找越乱。
老师让学生先别急着写结论，而是先根据看到的现象自己创建一个解释，再互相问哪里站不住。
医院准备创建新的预约系统时，最先去问的不是技术公司，而是天天在窗口接电话的那几个护士。

example_translations.translation: The new coworker spent an entire afternoon setting up the shared folder, and while doing it also named each category of materials separately so that later on everyone would not get more and more confused while searching.

The teacher told the students not to rush to write a conclusion, but to first create an explanation of their own based on what they observed and then question one another about where it failed to hold up.
When the hospital prepared to build a new appointment system, the first people they asked were not the tech companies but the nurses who answer calls at the service window every day.

glosses.notes: Often used for formally founding an institution, organization, system, or enduring initiative with a clear beginning.

examples.sentence: 这所学校刚创立时连像样的操场都没有，可是第一批老师下课以后还是会留下来帮学生把桌子和椅子修好。
他总说自己创立公司那几年最难的不是借钱，而是明明心里没底，还得每天先让大家安心上班。
这个奖学金是以前的学生为纪念老师才创立的，所以每年公布名单以前，大家都会先把老师当年的故事再讲一遍。

example_translations.translation: When this school was first established, it did not even have a proper sports field, but after class the first group of teachers would still stay behind to help the students repair the desks and chairs.

He always says that in the years when he founded the company, the hardest part was not borrowing money, but having to make everyone feel secure enough to keep working even when he himself felt unsure.

This scholarship was formally set up by the teacher's former students in memory of that teacher, so every year before the names are announced, people first retell the stories from that teacher's time.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to an original idea that gives a design, event, product, or solution a fresh and memorable angle.

examples.sentence: 客户原来只要一张普通海报，可是她听完活动安排以后突然冒出个创意，决定把整面墙都做成大家能写字的留言板。
导演知道钱不多，所以每次有人提创意，他先不问好不好看，只问现场能不能在一天里真的搭出来。
这家面包店能一直让人记住，不只是味道稳定，还因为老板总会在节日前想出一点不夸张的小创意。

example_translations.translation: The client had originally wanted only an ordinary poster, but after hearing the event plan she suddenly came up with a creative idea and decided to turn the whole wall into a message board that everyone could write on.
The director knows there is not much money, so whenever someone suggests a concept, the first question is not whether it looks good but whether it can really be built on site within one day.
This bakery has remained memorable not only because the taste is steady, but also because before every holiday the owner comes up with a small creative touch that is fresh without being excessive.

glosses.notes: Describes something going straight up and down, or standing at a right angle to a horizontal surface or line.

examples.sentence: 师傅看他量了半天还在犹豫，就把一根细线挂下来让他看，墙角只有真正垂直，后面的柜子装上去才不会慢慢歪掉。
门一开，她抬头看见一面垂直绿墙从一楼一直长到顶层，连本来急着开会的人都忍不住多看了两眼。
老师说，手一动，画里的线就算看着垂直，也会让人觉得楼不直。

example_translations.translation: Seeing him measure for a long time and still hesitate, the craftsperson hung down a thin line to show him that only if the corner is truly vertical will the cabinet installed afterward avoid slowly leaning out of shape.

As soon as the door opened, she looked up and saw a vertical green wall growing all the way from the first floor to the top, and even the people who had been in a hurry to get to a meeting could not help taking a second look.
The teacher said that once the hand moved, the lines in the picture could still look vertical while making the building seem not straight.

glosses.notes: Means pure or not mixed with other things, and when used adverbially it can mean entirely or simply for one reason.

examples.sentence: 老人一喝就说这碗豆浆味道很纯，没有加太多东西，所以连平时嫌淡的孩子都跟着多喝了半杯。
她学画画不是纯为了拿奖，而是一下雨就想坐在窗边把街上来回走的人慢慢画下来。
这块白布在灯下看着很纯，但是一拿到阳台上跟旧布一比，大家才发现它其实还带一点淡黄。

example_translations.translation: The older man took one sip and said the soy milk tasted very pure, without too many extra things added, so even the child who usually complains that it is bland ended up drinking another half cup.
She did not study painting purely to win prizes. Whenever it rains, she simply wants to sit by the window and slowly draw the people moving back and forth on the street.

This piece of white cloth looked very pure under the lamp, but once it was taken to the balcony and compared with an old piece of cloth, everyone realized it actually still carried a faint yellow tint.

glosses.notes: Refers to porcelain objects such as bowls, plates, vases, and other pieces fired from fine clay and often kept or collected with care.

examples.sentence: 那几件老瓷器本来放在里面，可是老板刚讲完它们怎么做，门口的人就慢慢往前走，想看清上面的图。
奶奶搬家时最不放心的不是衣服，而是柜子里那几件旧瓷器，所以一路上都让父亲把车开得特别慢。
老板怕客人只把瓷器放着看，就拿出一个旧碗，说以前一家人都用它吃饭。

example_translations.translation: Those old porcelain pieces had originally been placed farther inside, but as soon as the owner finished explaining how they were made, the people at the door slowly walked forward to look more clearly at the design on them.
When Grandma moved house, what worried her most was not the clothes but the old pieces of porcelain in the cabinet, so all along the way she kept telling Father to drive especially slowly.
Afraid customers would only look at the porcelain as something to display, the owner took out an old bowl and said that in the past a whole family used it for meals.

glosses.notes: Used for the exact present moment, often when someone becomes especially aware of what is happening or what must be decided now.

examples.sentence: 她站在门口等结果的时候，脑子里反而特别安静，只觉得此刻连楼道里那只老钟的声音都比平时清楚。
如果你此刻就想走，我不会拦你，可是至少先把那张表填完，别让后面的人又白等一下午。
广播里刚念到他们那一组的名字，他才第一次意识到，此刻再低头改鞋带已经来不及了。

example_translations.translation: As she stood at the door waiting for the result, her mind became strangely calm, and she felt that at this moment even the sound of the old clock in the hallway was clearer than usual.
If you want to leave right now, I will not stop you, but at least finish filling out that form first and do not make the people behind you wait the whole afternoon for nothing again.
Only when the announcement read out their group's name did he realize for the first time that at this moment it was already too late to lower his head and retie his shoelace.

glosses.notes: As a verb it means to prick, poke, or stab into something; as a noun it can refer to a thorn or sharp point on a plant or object.

examples.sentence: 树枝从墙外伸进来，正好刺到她晾在阳台边的衣服，等她发现时，布上已经多了一道小口子。
医生说伤口不深，像是被细东西刺了一下，但是父亲还是不放心，一路都看着孩子的手。
这朵花远看很安静，可是枝上全是硬刺，所以那个人包花时又加了一层纸，怕客人一拿就伤到手。

example_translations.translation: A branch stretched in from outside the wall and pricked the clothes she had hung by the balcony, and by the time she noticed, there was already a small tear in the fabric.
The doctor said the wound was not deep and looked as if some thin thing had stabbed it once, but Father was still uneasy and kept watching the child's hand all the way back.

From a distance the flower looked calm and delicate, but the branch was full of hard thorns, so that person added another layer of paper while wrapping the flowers, afraid a customer would hurt a hand the moment they picked it up.

glosses.notes: Used when counting how many times something happens, especially repeated actions, failures, visits, or interruptions.

examples.sentence: 这台旧机器最近出问题的次数越来越多，修理的人每次刚把工具收好，隔两天又会被车间叫回来。
医生看了记录以后说，他夜里醒来的次数要是再增加，就不能只靠早睡来解决，最好尽快再做一次检查。
她不是记不住台词，而是排练次数太少，所以一听到台下有人走动，眼神就会一下子乱掉。

example_translations.translation: The number of times this old machine has been breaking down has been rising lately. Every time the repair workers finish packing their tools, the workshop calls them back again two days later.

After looking at the record, the doctor said that if the number of times he wakes up at night increases any further, the problem cannot be solved just by going to bed early and another checkup should be done soon.
It is not that she cannot memorize the lines. The problem is that the number of rehearsals has been too small, so the moment she hears someone moving under the stage, her gaze goes scattered at once.

glosses.notes: Describes doing something quickly and with a sense that there is not enough time to finish it calmly or properly.

examples.sentence: 他匆匆吃了两口早饭就往车站跑，到了站台才发现自己拿错了包，里面全是女儿下午上课要用的画纸。
两个人在医院门口匆匆说了几句就分开了，一个回去照顾老人，一个赶去单位把请假的事补清楚。
她本来想把解释写长一点，可是通知来得太突然，只能匆匆留下一张纸条，连最后一句都没写完整。

example_translations.translation: He ate two hurried bites of breakfast and ran to the station, only to discover on the platform that he had grabbed the wrong bag and that it was full of the drawing paper his daughter needed for class that afternoon.

The two people exchanged only a few words in haste at the hospital entrance before separating, with one going back to care for an older family member and the other hurrying to the office to settle the leave request properly.
She had wanted to write a longer explanation, but the notice came too suddenly, so she could only hurriedly leave a short note and did not even finish the final sentence.

glosses.notes: Describes a state of being pressed for time, often in a way that makes actions or decisions feel incomplete or careless.

examples.sentence: 因为出门太匆忙，他把两只不一样的鞋都穿上了，走到门口才发现，低头一看自己也笑了。
这份决定看着像临时做的，其实前面已经讨论了很久，只是消息公布得太匆忙，外面的人一时还看不出来。
她不喜欢在匆忙里答应别人的请求，所以每次有人突然把事推到面前，她都会先把时间表翻出来再说。

example_translations.translation: Because he left home in such a hurry, he put on two different shoes and only noticed when he reached the door, then lowered his head and laughed at himself.
This decision looks as if it was made at the last minute, but in fact it had been discussed for a long time. It is only that the news was announced too hastily for outsiders to see that at once.
She does not like agreeing to other people's requests while in a rush, so whenever someone suddenly pushes a matter in front of her, she first opens her schedule before answering.

glosses.notes: A more formal way to say that something has never happened up to now, often used for emphasis in narration or reflection.

examples.sentence: 父亲嘴上总说自己什么都见过，但是那天站在海边看见天一下子黑下来，他还是承认自己从未碰到过那样急的风。
她从未想过多年以后会在旧同学开的店里再见面，所以刚推门进去时，连该先叫名字还是先笑都拿不准。
这位老师批评人一直很直接，但是学生都知道，他从未拿谁家里的难处当成公开说笑的话题。

example_translations.translation: Father always says he has seen everything, but that day, standing by the sea and watching the sky suddenly go dark, he still admitted that he had never encountered such fierce wind.

She had never imagined that many years later she would see an old classmate again in a shop that classmate opened, so when she pushed the door and went in, she could not even decide whether to call the name first or smile first.
This teacher has always criticized people directly, but the students all know that he has never turned anyone's family hardships into a topic for public joking.

glosses.notes: Used in formal or semi-formal contexts to describe working in a particular line of professional or industry-related work.

examples.sentence: 她从业十几年以后才明白，真正留住客人的不只是把流程说清，而是别人着急时你能不能把话说得让人安心。
刚从业的人常觉得不难，但是真想做好，还得会看人。
父亲年轻时从业于海上运输，公司一忙就是好几个月不回家，所以他现在最怕孩子找一份天天见不到太阳的工作。

example_translations.translation: Only after working in the profession for more than ten years did she understand that what truly keeps customers is not just explaining the process clearly, but whether you can speak in a way that reassures them when they are anxious.
People who are new to the profession often think it is not hard, but if they really want to do it well, they still have to know how to read people.

When Father was young, he was professionally employed in sea transport, and whenever the company got busy he would not come home for months, so now he most fears his child taking a job where you hardly see daylight.
